lede: You asked for a questionnaire on intimacy and explicit scenes: courtship and relationships by culture, desire and refusal lines, dubcon handling, aftermath, how bonds grow and the new style in bed, with three research passes (the current law, the house archive, and erotic and romantic craft across Western, Eastern and LitRPG writing) behind every option and sample. There are 43 questions in four sections, every sample is between adults, and nothing the Style Law or the Combat Law ruled is asked again: the settled list at the end says what was left alone and why. Answer the five Keystones first, since most later questions lean on them; every question carries a recommendation you can take as it stands.

question.title: Reading a lover
question.question: When a lover can read the other by faculty, nose or eye, may that read run in bed without leave?
question.context: The archive's commonest intimate device is a lover read as an instrument: a nose, fate threads, a pulse counted down. A faculty read prints exact figures when the reader's Gnosis Perception outranks the target's Resilience Ward by Grade (R71-44); a scenting POV reads by smell (R71-63); clansmen believe the Moto read through the eyes (R53-15). Nothing says whether reading a lover unasked is intimacy or trespass.

options.label: Lovers read freely
options.consequence: Any sense or faculty runs in bed as it runs anywhere; the read is part of how desire and refusal show (SC7), and being read is part of being a lover.
options.sample: Wenna had Ansel on his back with his cock deep in her, and rode him slow while the draw-hum ran under the floorboards. Her faculty opened as easily as her thighs had, and his figures came up behind her eyes in the Guild's own columns: reserve low from the day's work, his Ward lying open. She had not asked. Lovers didn't. She bent and set her teeth to the side of his throat, and he came with a sound like a man struck.

options.label: Every read by leave
options.consequence: Any read past the ordinary senses waits on leave, in words or body; one taken unasked is trespass, felt by the one read as its tell, stopped by a Ward, and entered on the Ledger once found (K5).
options.sample: Wenna had Ansel on his back with his cock deep in her, and rode him slow while the draw-hum ran under the floorboards. She touched two fingers to his temple. "May I?" He thought about it with his hips still moving under her. "Go on." Her faculty opened, and his figures came up behind her eyes in the Guild's own columns: reserve low from the day's work, his Ward lying open because he had laid it open. She said nothing of what she saw.

options.label: Senses free, workings by leave
options.consequence: What cannot shut, a beastkin nose or ears, reads freely; a worked read, by Gnosis or a Moto's eyes, needs leave, and one taken unasked is B's trespass, with B's tell, counter and debt.
options.sample: Wenna's nose had told her Ansel wanted her before the door was shut, and nobody asks leave of a nose. The faculty was another matter. With his cock deep in her and her hips slowing, she touched two fingers to his temple. "May I?" "No," said Ansel. She took her fingers away, and her ears came forward. She smelled the fear go out of his sweat and the want come back into it, and rode him harder for the answer.

question.rec_reason: A nose cannot be asked to stop, so B would make every beastkin lover a trespasser by breathing; a worked read is a choice, so it can carry the tell, the counter and the bill that every ability owes.

question.title: Bedchamber arts
question.question: May the act itself carry a working, Essence given, pooled or drawn between the partners?
question.context: China's fangzhongshu (the arts of the bedchamber) treat sex as cultivation: conserve jing (vital essence) and draw on the partner's; xianxia (immortal-cultivation fiction) turns it into dual cultivation, a power-up. Fracture of Worlds gives bonds mechanical weight (the Axis Sub-Stat, the Spirit Axis) but no working through the act, and Yorime's Claim (drawing Essence out of a target) works by touch. SC8 asks only about desire.

options.label: Never through the act
options.consequence: Sex moves no Essence. Bonds grow only by CO15's routes, the Crystal takes no notice of a bed, and a Claim by touch stays a Claim, never a lovers' art.

options.label: Given, never drawn
options.consequence: A bedchamber art may give or pool what both partners offer, built under ability law with a cost in both bodies, a tell and a counter; no art draws from a partner in bed.

options.label: Given or drawn, fully priced
options.consequence: A bedchamber art is a technique: a Codex line, a cost in both bodies, a tell, a counter, no figure until canon holds one. One drawing unasked is a Claim, and the scene dubcon or non-con (SC8).

question.rec_reason: Your xianxia and progression models live on such arts, and C holds them to the fairness every ability meets, a cost, a tell, a counter and no invented figure, while a drawing art becomes a dark engine a player can find and stop.

question.title: The pleasure trade
question.question: Does the Draw Age keep a trade in sex on the page, and in what form?
question.context: Nothing in canon names a brothel, a courtesan or a bathhouse, and the price table has no row for one, though money comes before magic (R53-17). Victorian Britain inspected women under the Contagious Diseases Acts (1864 to 1869, repealed 1886) and held them in lock hospitals (locked venereal wards); Edo's Yoshiwara ranked its courtesans; Joseon's gisaeng were state-registered entertainers trained in verse.

options.label: Each culture's own form
options.consequence: The Accord licenses houses under seal and inspection, Eastern courts keep ranked quarters or verse-trained entertainers, the north keeps no house and trades in kind; entered in CO1's Mores field, fees as price-table rows on your word.
options.sample: Mother Fettle's house on Tallow Row kept its licence framed by the door under green wax, with the inspector's last mark inked beside it, and a girl would show her own card if a man asked. Dunstan didn't ask. He paid the fee chalked over the hatch and went up. North of the arrays there was no house and no paper. The same bargain was a skin of seal fat at somebody's fire, with nobody's mark on it.

options.label: One licence everywhere
options.consequence: A single licence, seal and inspection runs wherever the licensing Guilds' conduit runs: proof-marked houses, one fee list, inspectors who take bribes; a cheaper unlicensed trade works beside it.
options.sample: Mother Fettle's house on Tallow Row kept its licence framed by the door under green wax, the same seal that hung in every licensed house from the Accord's ports to the Seat. Dunstan paid the fee chalked over the hatch, the Guild's own figure, and went up. Out past the last conduit the women who would not pay for a seal worked the inn yards for less, and the inspectors drank there free.

options.label: Texture, never a house
options.consequence: The trade lives in talk, the Rumor Mill and a scene's edges; no house is entered, no fee priced, and no explicit scene is set in one.
options.sample: Dunstan knew the house on Tallow Row the way everyone in the ward knew it: from the draymen's talk at the standpipe, from the chaplain's sermons, from the green lamp that burned there after the meters were read. He walked past it twice that winter with his hands in his pockets. What went on behind the lamp stayed a thing men said, and some of what they said was wrong.

question.rec_reason: It answers CO1's Mores field with each culture's own form, gives money before magic a trade it has ignored, and puts fees, debts, the pox and gossip where the Ledger can collect them; B flattens every culture into the Accord.

settled_extra.why_not_asked: World texture law; CO18 asks only whether the Draw Age keeps a trade in sex and in what form.
